spec_match.rationale: Calls the real Element.setHTML(raw) with the default sanitizer on CfT 153 (shipped, enabled by default in 146); serialized output shows scripts, on* handlers, javascript: hrefs, style attrs and svg <script> removed.

interactive.rationale: Three presets plus a free textarea and Sanitize & render produce live rendered and serialized output from the native sanitizer.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index card promises stripping of scripts, handlers and javascript: hrefs while keeping safe markup, which is exactly what the page does.

edge_cases.rationale: The tricky preset covers svg script, unquoted handlers, leading-space javascript:, comments and MathML, but the strip log is a regex over raw text: plain text 'one = 1' reports '⚠ still present: inline event handlers (check browser version)' — a false positive with misleading upgrade copy.

references.rationale: Cites chromestatus.com/feature/5814067399491584 and MDN; no spec link.

conformance.rationale: Feature suite 7/7 PASS on CfT 153 including a behavioural setHTML script-strip check, parseHTML, setHTMLUnsafe and Sanitizer.get().

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12 driven by Node Playwright (chromium.launch) against a local server on :3111 — NOT chrome-devtools-mcp, which is unavailable in this environment, so this is not DevTools-MCP-verified evidence; no accessibility-tree dump was taken. All presets and Sanitize driven, zero console errors/failed requests, 0px overflow both classes — but the strip log is visibly broken: after sanitizing the XSS preset it shows only '✗ stripped:' because the label '<script>' is interpolated into innerHTML and opens a real <script> element that swallows the rest of the log (screenshot el_xss_log.png).

telemetry_health.rationale: Only shared runtime/console capture; no assertion that setHTML actually removed the payload.

accessibility.rationale: Textarea has an aria-label (placeholder-copy), but output/serialized/log panels are not live regions and panel labels are plain divs not tied to the regions.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: 0px overflow both classes; 4 of 5 controls under 44px on mobile.

openQuestions.title: Fix the strip log: '<script>' label is parsed as markup
openQuestions.detail: Repro: load, click Sanitize & render → log shows only '✗ stripped:'. dangerPatterns labels like '<script>', '<iframe>', '<embed>/<object>' are interpolated into stripLog.innerHTML, creating a real <script> that swallows the following spans. Build log entries with textContent.

openQuestions.title: Derive the stripped list from DOM diff, not regex, and drop 'check browser version'
openQuestions.detail: Repro: input 'one = 1 and x' → '⚠ still present: inline event handlers (check browser version)'. Compare parsed input vs sanitized DOM (or Document.parseHTMLUnsafe vs parseHTML) and never blame browser age when setHTML is present.

openQuestions.title: Remove a11y-fixer pollution from the payload presets
openQuestions.detail:
The XSS preset's

now carries role="button" tabindex="0" onkeydown="…this.click()" — an automated fixer rewrote the hostile sample. Restore the original payload string.

openQuestions.title: Show Document.parseHTML and setHTMLUnsafe contrast
openQuestions.detail: Spec surfaces Document.parseHTML (sanitized, inspect-before-insert) and setHTMLUnsafe/parseHTMLUnsafe (opt-in, still configurable); a concept comparing them shows the safe/unsafe split and why unsafe elements can't be re-allowed through setHTML.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use setHTML()/Document.parseHTML() with a Sanitizer config of the current shape (elements, attributes, replaceWithChildrenElements); elements not in `elements` are removed with their content; unsafe elements cannot be re-allowed via setHTML.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Followed for the sanitization itself (native setHTML default).

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Never interpolate user-controlled strings into innerHTML; use textContent or DOM construction.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Not followed — log labels interpolated into innerHTML create a live <script> element.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Announce asynchronous/changing results through a polite live region (role=status/log or aria-live) and keep controls as native buttons with accessible names.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Not followed — results are not announced.

summary: The core demo is genuine — native setHTML on the shipped API with good hostile presets — but its 'what was stripped' log is broken by its own <script> label being parsed as HTML, and it uses regex heuristics that produce false positives with misleading upgrade copy.
